Blintzes

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Serves 6Prep 25 minCook 20 min

Blintzes are thin, crepe-like pancakes filled with sweetened cheese or fruit, traditionally served during Yom Kippur to break the fast. They symbolize renewal and sweetness for the year ahead, making them a cherished dish for this solemn holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup all-purpose flour (120 g)
  • 1 cup milk (240 ml)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil or melted butter (30 ml)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup farmer's cheese or ricotta (240 g)
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar (50 g)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup sour cream (120 ml), for serving
  • Butter or oil for frying

Method

  1. In a mixing bowl, whisk together flour, milk, eggs, vegetable oil, and salt until smooth to make the batter.
  2. Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and lightly grease it with butter or oil.
  3. Pour about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of batter into the skillet, swirling to spread it thinly and evenly.
  4. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the edges lift and the bottom is lightly golden, then carefully flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds. Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter.
  5. In a separate bowl, combine farmer's cheese, sugar, and vanilla extract until smooth.
  6. Place a tablespoon of the cheese filling near the edge of each crepe, fold in the sides, and roll up to enclose the filling.
  7. Heat butter in the skillet over medium heat. Fry the filled blintzes seam side down for 2-3 minutes until golden, then carefully flip and cook the other side for another 2 minutes.
  8. Serve warm topped with sour cream.

Tips

  • For a fruit variation, substitute the cheese filling with sweetened mashed berries or applesauce.
  • Use a non-stick skillet for easier crepe cooking and flipping.
  • Blintzes can be made ahead and refrigerated; reheat gently in a skillet before serving.
